name: Kusunda
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Watters, David E. (with Yogendra P. Yadava, Madhav P. Pokharel, Balaram Prasain). 2006. Notes on Kusunda Grammar: A language isolate of Nepal. Himalayan Linguistics Archive 3, pp. 1-182 (first ed. 2005, NFDIN, Kathmandu). DOI 10.5070/H90023671, https://escholarship.org/uc/item/83v8d1wv
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Ch. 4 Phonology (pp. 22-43) has no stress/accent/suprasegmental section and never states where stress falls; the only stress mention is a passing remark on p. 32 (§4.4.1) that the p/b voicing contrast is sometimes neutralized intervocalically 'especially in rapid speech and if the syllable in question is unstressed'. Pitch is discussed only as a concomitant lowering under pharyngealization before voiced uvulars (§4.3.2, p. 26) and as falling-rising pitch on the negative suffix -aˤu (§5.5.4.1, §6.1.2.2).

sources.citation: Spendley, Augie. 2024. Possessive prefixes in Proto-Kusunda. Himalayan Linguistics 23(1). DOI 10.5070/h923161179
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Morphological reconstruction from Hodgson 1857 and Reinhard & Toba 1970 data; no mention of stress, accent, tone or pitch.

sources.citation: Aaley, Uday Raj & Timotheus A. Bodt. 2020. New Kusunda data: A list of 250 concepts. Computer-Assisted Language Comparison in Practice 3.4; CLDF dataset lexibank/aaleykusunda (Zenodo 3746946)
sources.note: Blog post + 662-form IPA wordlist (GM, K, Proto-Kusunda); forms carry syllable dots but no stress marks (0 occurrences of ˈ); no statement on stress.

sources.citation: Aaley, Uday Raj & Timotheus A. Bodt. 2019. New data on Kusunda. Humanities Commons (report, 3 pp.). DOI 10.17613/1zy2-k376
